Hold your phone firmly and make two quick chopping motions, mainly within the physical plane of the screen: side to side or up and down. Motions mainly toward or away from the screen are rejected. Never throw the phone or force the movement.

Keep the top of the phone uncovered: detection pauses when the proximity sensor is covered, including by your hand. A working proximity sensor is required.

Start at 50. Lower values require firmer movement; higher values accept lighter gestures. Your saved 0–100 setting is unchanged, but the new detector may feel different.

A silent notification keeps the service visible. “Active” means the service is running, not that detection during deep sleep is guaranteed. Screen-off reliability and battery use have not been measured.\n\nIf enabled, Android may restore detection after process loss, restart (after first unlock) or update. Stop, force-stop, denied notifications or battery restrictions require enabling again. No automatic retry loop.
Android battery optimization applies. If detection stops, check this app’s battery settings. An exemption is optional and does not guarantee detection during sleep.
Battery optimization exemption is enabled. This does not guarantee detection during sleep or low battery use.
No network, ads or analytics. Movements are processed in memory, never recorded or exported.

ChopTorch uses Android’s linear acceleration sensor (sensor fusion, without gravity) and proximity sensor in the background with a silent notification. Your choice is saved for recovery after process loss, restart (after first unlock) or update when Android allows it. Stop here or from the notification. Battery use has not been measured.
User-enabled detection, without sound or a permanent wake lock.
